Definition: middle voice from G4862 and the base of G2237; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning:--delight.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says he delights in the law of God after the inward man, even while another law in his members wars against him. The delight is real and inward, and it survives the war: the new man loves God's law even when the old man fights it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that delight in God's law is the mark of the inward man, and I believe this delight is the proof the Spirit has made me new.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
